B05.title: Rust Transactions, Pool Recovery, and Unknown
B05.boundary_and_ownership: Own transaction lifecycle/outcome/recovery and connection disposition policy in native/database/transactions; provider hooks remain B01 interfaces. Keep response-loss uncertainty out of generic Core status definitions.
B05.native_reuse: SQLx transaction/savepoint/pool mechanics and native provider hooks. SeaORM TransactionTrait is only relevant to an explicit specialized profile, not mandatory for ordinary adapters.
B05.csharp_surface: DataSession.BeginTransactionAsync, DataTransaction and Savepoint; TransactionOutcome/TransactionState/DatabaseCloseResult snapshots preserve Unknown and local cleanup separately. CommitAsync succeeds only for Committed; DatabaseException, CommitOutcomeUnknownException and DatabaseCleanupException retain their specified distinctions. DisposeAsync joins actual local safety; no business-delegate replay.
implementation_steps: Implement exactly the D15 four independent dimensions: TxLifecycle Active/Failed/CommitInFlight/RollbackInFlight/Closed; TransactionOutcome InProgress/Committed/RolledBack/Unknown; ConnectionDisposition Usable/ProviderResetPending/Quarantined/Discarded; LocalLifetime Live/Closing/Quiescent/Reclaimed. Private internal states require an explicit mapping and may not weaken these public observations.

The CommitAsync admission token can reject before the conservative provider-commit dispatch boundary. After entering CommitInFlight, use a separate finite commit deadline; request cancellation or loss of a trustworthy reply cannot replace Unknown with Cancelled or RolledBack. Reject Commit while Failed and distinguish trustworthy COMMIT confirmation from failed-transaction termination.

Run rollback/drain/probe through cleanup admission on the original session. Known ordered provider maintenance may be ProviderResetPending; unknown protocol damage is Quarantined and cannot be loaned to another tenant. Return the permit only when reuse is safe or physical retirement has completed; close_on_drop is intent, not observed retirement.

For unconfirmed rollback without any COMMIT attempt, expose Closed/InProgress, CommitAttempted=false, Cleanup=RollbackUnconfirmed and quarantine. After a previous Unknown COMMIT, every later cleanup rollback or no-transaction response leaves Unknown unchanged. Preserve primary and cleanup errors separately.

Implement explicit savepoint stack/generation and isolation capabilities on the same session. SQLite Deferred/Immediate is not a PostgreSQL isolation matrix; unsupported levels fail before begin. Ordinary commands cannot change transaction ownership through raw transaction-control SQL.

CloseAsync closes public admission, requests or joins already-admitted transaction/cursor cleanup and may return Pending with LocalResourcesReleased=false. The Engine retains parents, callbacks, roots and budgets until safe retirement. DisposeAsync joins the same cleanup and cannot claim success while access remains possible; synchronous Dispose only transfers cleanup responsibility without blocking a finalizer.

Propagate recovery ID and D20 tenant/key/request-hash identity without creating an automatic business retry service. PG ReadCommitted conflict recovery uses a subsequent SELECT statement; one missing same-statement CTE result or cleanup completion never proves rollback. Persist uncertainty separately from releasable native owners.

B08.title: Rust Migration Execution and Version Ledger
B08.boundary_and_ownership: Own explicit deployment migration runner and ledger policy; never automatic destructive schema synchronization in ordinary DataSource startup. Keep administration pools/sessions separate from request transactions.
B08.native_reuse: SQLx Migrator/Migrate, native migration checksums, provider transactional DDL and ledger. Provider-specific locking is inspected, not assumed identical.
B08.csharp_surface: Migration, MigrationBundle, MigrationOptions, MigrationStatus, MigrationReport, SchemaColumn, SchemaTable and DatabaseAdministration.MigrateAsync/GetMigrationStatusAsync/ValidateMigrationsAsync/GetTablesAsync; explicit SQL scripts, checksums, ordered native ledger and provider transaction/locking limits.
implementation_steps: Build the migration manifest from trusted application/admin artifacts, not untrusted table-name strings. Stable same-ID/same-hash succeeds idempotently; changed hash rejects.
For PostgreSQL, execute on a dedicated admin connection. Migrator error paths can return before session advisory unlock; close the connection on every exit path, and prove lock disappearance.

For SQLite, SQLx lock/unlock is a no-op. Reject no_tx entries before admission, use Connection::begin_with("BEGIN IMMEDIATE") to obtain a depth-tracked Transaction, and Migrator::run(&mut *tx). Explicitly commit success or rollback error, retaining cleanup failure and closing a damaged connection. Never raw query BEGIN: it bypasses SQLx depth and causes nested-BEGIN error. Serialize checksum/DDL/ledger under the writer lock.

Initial supported profile is transactional migrations. Statements incompatible with that transaction are explicitly rejected or require a separately specified recovery-phase profile; never label partially executed DDL atomic.
Persist exact migration/hash/provider/phase and define crash/resume behavior without treating a connection-close success as unknown business commit resolution.

SQLite WAL does not serialize concurrent migrators by itself; test busy timeout and acquiring the writer lock before history reads.
Cancellation must complete native cleanup and release or close the administrative connection; no implicit schema repair on startup.
specific_acceptance: Real PG session advisory lock remains after checksum error then disappears on dedicated close; test permission failure, cancellation, changed checksum and new-process resume.
Two independent SQLite migration runners contend: one complete ledger+DDL result, no duplicate or contradictory history; rollback failing DDL, repeat apply and mismatched checksum.

Preserve the independent three-case raw-BEGIN negative, tracked outer commit/rollback, and failed-second-migration all-batch rollback oracles. Cross-process contention, crash/recovery, Windows and the actual C# AOT wrapper remain product conformance.
